article.title: Russia's own figures show it has lost nearly 500,000 people in Ukraine war
article.summary:
At least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died since the start of the war in Ukraine in 2022, according to Russian government statistics analysed by the BBC.
The leaked Rosstat data reveal how the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has fundamentally changed mortality patterns in Russia, and show the high cost paid in human life in a war that Vladimir Putin had assumed would last only days but is now almost five years old.
Russia's statistics agency admitted to a cyber-attack, but denied any protected information had been leaked.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Wednesday that only Russia's defence ministry could officially report data on losses: "I suggest no other data be taken into account."
The defence ministry has not released any official casualty figures for several years.

article.title: What Australia’s ‘Digital Duty of Care’ Law Means for Big Tech
article.summary:
Under the Digital Duty of Care law, platforms must provide risk assessments to regulators at least once a year, and they must notify regulators before they introduce significant changes to their platforms that could allow for new risks of harm, such as “addictive” design features.
The amendments also make it easier for Australian citizens to hold tech companies to account.
Previously, one needed to rely on complex legal avenues concerning company negligence and consumer protection.
The new law grants Australians the “private right of action,” which means they can directly sue digital platforms for breaching their duty of care.
